goal: The Pythagorean theorem EARNED: a real face opens the question, the four-triangle rearrangement proves a² + b² = c² in front of you, an end card lands it.
audience: anyone who memorized the formula and never saw why
assumptions: 50-70s of finished piece across BOTH formats (16:9 + 9:16, re-compositions not crops)
the opening real clip is the studio's recorded public-domain NASA talking-head fixture (real footage, licensed, in-repo)
the proof is the four-triangle rearrangement (visual, not algebraic)
every number on screen is a sympy claim
one design system across all three segments; the seams are designed

decision.why: The piece needs what no single technique has: real footage for the open (edit), a narrated verified visual proof (math — the claims and the narration clock), and a designed end card (motion). The assembler joins them with a designed seam.

alternatives.rejected_because: a pure math film cannot open on real footage — the request's first ask

alternatives.id: simplest: one math film with a text card open and close
alternatives.rejected_because: the simplest thing that could work — but 'a real clip' is the request's opening word, and a text card is not a clip

segments.role: the cold open: a real face asks why
segments.brief: The NASA talking-head clip, cut to its strongest 8 seconds, captioned, ending on the question the proof will answer.
acceptance: real footage (the licensed fixture, never a re-enactment)

segments.brief: The four-triangle rearrangement: the square of the hypotenuse, the two squares of the legs, the same four triangles inside both — a² + b² = c² seen, not asserted. Narrated; every number a claim.
acceptance: the rearrangement is animated (both dissections shown)
every number is a sympy claim
the narration clock drives the scenes

segments.brief: The theorem statement a² + b² = c² landing, the three-square echo of the proof, the studio mark.
acceptance: the card carries the theorem + the mark
8s, one beat in and one out

assembly.transitions: designed seams (a shape carries across each cut — never black)
assembly.audio: one mix: the clip's dialog, then the narration, at one loudness

risks: the composite seam must be designed (the probe)
the proof must read in BOTH formats (the 9:16 re-composition of a geometric proof is the hard part)
